messages:
From: Maya Singh <maya@novum.ai>

Cc: Novum Contracts <contracts@novum.ai>
Date: Wed, 01 Oct 2025 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft order form + redlines (IP & productization concerns)

Hi Ben,

Thanks for the demo last week — Novum is excited about Redwood's latency profile. Attached is our version of the order form with redlines (redlines_novum_v3.pdf) and a short evidence request (evidence-ip-workflow.xlsx). High level items we care about:

- Output ownership: we flagged language that suggests assignment of derivative rights. For our use case we need clarity that Novum gets perpetual title to customer-facing product outputs in which we invest.
- Training/data use: we ask for a carveout preventing Redwood from using Novum content to further train public models (we suggested a "no-training" clause unless explicit opt-in and/or paid license).
- Feedback/license: we included a clause to ensure feedback and telemetry we share can be used by Redwood for product improvement but not for model retraining without consent.

Could you confirm Redwood's default position on each of these? If you have a standard compromise (e.g., non-exclusive license for outputs + strict no-train by default), please share wording. We'd prefer to move quickly — would you be available for a 30m call tomorrow (10/2) to run through?

Attachments: Novum_OrderForm_v3.docx, redlines_novum_v3.pdf, evidence-ip-workflow.xlsx

Thanks,

Hi Maya — got the materials, thanks.

I'll loop in legal to get proposed language for the three buckets you called out. Short answers for now:
- Output ownership: Redwood does not typically assign model IP; we can grant a broad, perpetual, non-exclusive right to use output for Novum's products and allow limited productization for internal/external use per the order form.
- Training/data use: our standard is "no training on customer-provided content unless customer opts in" — we'll confirm exact retention/telemetry scope.
- Feedback/license: we usually take a non-exclusive product-improvement license that excludes training without explicit opt-in.

Happy to take a 30m call tomorrow at 11:00am PT. If that doesn't work, propose 3pm PT. I'll send a forward to legal with a short summary and ask for concrete clause proposals.

Cheers,

Subject: Fwd: Novum redlines — need legal wording for output/training/feedback (DEAL-4872)

Laura / Karthik — forwarding Novum's redlines for DEAL-4872 (Novum). They want stronger rights to outputs and a hard "no-training" carveout unless opt-in. They also propose a feedback license that excludes retraining.

Summary of asks (from Novum):
1) "Perpetual title to customer-facing outputs" — they may treat this as assignment for productization.
2) No training on customer content; telemetry may be used for debugging but not for model updates.
3) A feedback license that allows Redwood product improvements but explicitly prohibits model retrain without consent.

Our preliminary commercial stance (suggested):
- Keep model and underlying weights with Redwood. Do NOT agree to assignment.
- Offer Novum a broad, perpetual, non-exclusive, transferrable (to affiliates) license to use outputs and to productize outputs for their customers, but: exclude any right to the underlying model and exclude rights to use Novum data for training beyond an explicit opt-in.
- Accept a scoped feedback/telemetry license for product improvement (bug fixes, performance tuning) with an explicit clause prohibiting use of customer content for model training unless customer signs an addendum.
- As a compromise for Novum's concerns about evidence, offer a periodic telemetry summary (redacted) and an engineering evidence package (evidence-ip-workflow.xlsx) to satisfy procurement.

Action items: could you propose 1-2 clause drafts we can send back? I think we can resolve commercially if legal provides defensible language for the license carveouts and a short operational paragraph defining "training" vs "improvement".

Thanks — I'll be on the call with Novum tomorrow at 11:00am PT unless you prefer a pre-call sync.

— Ben

From: Maya Singh <maya@novum.ai>
To: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Novum Contracts <contracts@novum.ai>
Date: Fri, 03 Oct 2025 15:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft order form + redlines (IP & productization concerns)

Ben — thanks for the quick turnaround and for looping legal. After our internal review we can accept the following compromise if Redwood can commit in writing: 

1) Novum receives a perpetual, worldwide, non-exclusive license to use, modify, and distribute outputs generated by the service for Novum's commercial products. This permits productization but does NOT grant rights to Redwood's underlying model weights or training artifacts.

2) Redwood confirms in the order form that customer content and Novum-only prompts will NOT be used to train or further fine-tune any models by Redwood unless Novum provides explicit opt-in permission in a separate training agreement. Telemetry used for debugging/ops is ok if aggregated and redacted; we attached an evidence template (evidence-ip-workflow.xlsx) to illustrate needed artifacts.

3) Feedback license: Redwood may use aggregated/anonymous feedback for product improvement (performance, reliability), but must not use identifiable Novum content for model development without the separate opt-in. We propose explicit language and a 12-month retention cap for raw telemetry unless otherwise agreed.

If Redwood can accept those bullets, Novum will: (a) remove the assignment language from the order form, (b) produce a short countersigned order form, and (c) route procurement to finalize pricing. I've attached a redline reply (redlines_reply_v2.pdf) with the suggested replacement wording.

Can you route the proposed language from legal and confirm by EOD Monday so procurement can calendar signature next week?

Thanks,
Maya
Head of Procurement, Novum
maya@novum.ai
